title: Civil-society and Hong Konger groups' press conference on a Hong Kong rights clause
location: Room 101, Legislative Yuan Zhongxing Building (Committee Research Building), Taipei
scope: Local press conference in Taipei with policy demands to Taiwan's own government and separate appeals to foreign authorities
organizer: Hong Kong Outlanders in Taiwan; Taiwan Association for Human Rights; Economic Democracy Union; Taiwan Citizen Front; Taiwan Hong Kong Association; New School for Democracy; Taiwan Youth Association for Democracy; Covenants Watch; Judicial Reform Foundation
participants_original: A press conference is documented; no total attendee count is reported. Two Hong Kong speakers are identified as online participants.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. Organizer and news reports document a press conference with named speakers but give no onsite attendance count or evidence of a public gathering reaching 50 people.

title.summary: Organizer, CNA and Civil Media describe a Jan 8 press conference by Taiwan civil-society and Hong Konger groups.

start_date.summary: The organizer gives Jan 8 at 9 a.m.; same-day CNA and the Jan 13 Civil Media follow-up describe the conference on Jan 8.

end_date.summary: The pages do not report departure or physical dissolution; the scheduled time span is not treated as a physical end.

location.summary: Organizer and follow-up reports place the press conference in Room 101 of the Legislative Yuan's Zhongxing/Research Building in Taipei.

scope.summary: The reported gathering is at one Taipei venue; its stated calls include Taiwan policy and separate requests addressed to China/Hong Kong and the EU.

organizer.summary: The organizer release and Civil Media list the joint conveners: Hong Kong Outlanders in Taiwan, Taiwan Association for Human Rights, Economic Democracy Union, Taiwan Citizen Front, Taiwan Hong Kong Association, New School for Democracy, Taiwan Youth Association for Democracy, Covenants Watch and Judicial Reform Foundation.

demands.summary: The groups ask Taiwan's legislature/government to enact a Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Clause and formalize assistance to Hong Kongers; they also address demands to China/Hong Kong authorities and the EU. Available original categories do not clearly capture this rights-and-asylum policy demand, so the list remains empty.

participants_original.summary: The reports list speakers and indicate two Hong Kong participants joined online, but none reports a total onsite attendee count.

participants_min.summary: No numeric onsite turnout floor is published.

participants_max.summary: No numeric onsite turnout maximum is published.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The sources document a press conference and speakers only; no attendance estimate establishes at least 50 people.

protester_violence.summary: These accounts do not describe participant violence; silence is not used to infer its absence.

state_response.summary: The reports record demands but no event-specific state reception, refusal, or coercive response; each of the seven dimensions remains unknown.

eligibility.summary: A press conference with an explicit domestic Taiwan policy appeal occurred, but public protest/gathering status and attendance of at least 50 are unresolved.

notes: This is an organizer-reported press conference, not an established street demonstration. The demands include Taiwan's own government (a proposed Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Clause), so this is not treated as foreign-government-only solidarity; separate requests target Chinese/Hong Kong authorities and the EU. No turnout is inferred from organizations or online speakers.
